claims.quote: περὶ δὲ τοῦ συλλογίζεσθαι παντελῶς οὐδὲν εἴχομεν πρότερον ἄλλο λέγειν, ἀλλ᾽ ἢ τριβῇ ζητοῦντες πολὺν χρόνον ἐπονοῦμεν. (184b1–2)
claims.claim: The seated Greek of 184b1–2.

claims.quote: About syllogizing we had absolutely nothing else earlier to say, but were long at work seeking by practice.
claims.claim: #1574's translation of 184b1–2.

claims.quote: Ταύτης δὲ τῆς πραγματείας οὐ τὸ μὲν ἦν τὸ δ᾽ οὐκ ἦν προεξειργασμένον, ἀλλ᾽ οὐδὲν παντελῶς ὑπῆρχεν. (183b34–36)
claims.claim: The seated Greek of 183b34–36.

claims.quote: Of this inquiry, it was not that one part had been worked out beforehand and another had not; rather, nothing at all was there.
claims.claim: #1574's translation of 183b34–36.

claims.quote: οὐ negates τὸ μὲν ἦν τὸ δ᾽ οὐκ ἦν προεξειργασμένον. ἀλλά introduces οὐδὲν παντελῶς ὑπῆρχεν. οὐδέν is the subject of ὑπῆρχεν. παντελῶς follows it. προεξειργασμένον occurs once in the treatise.
claims.claim: οὐ negates the partial case; ἀλλά introduces the total; οὐδέν is the subject; προεξειργασμένον is a hapax in the treatise.
claims.lineage: the denial is total within its domain

claims.quote: 183b7–8 says that this second task is why Socrates asked but did not answer: he agreed that he did not know
claims.claim: Socrates is named inside the definition of the inquiry, as the reason for its second task.

claims.quote: 183b34–35 says that this inquiry is not of that kind: it was not that one part had been worked out beforehand and another had not.
claims.claim: The partly-worked-out case the sentence denies is rhetoric's case.
claims.lineage: the provenance axis of the paragraph

claims.quote: παντελῶς occurs three times in the treatise, all in this chapter
claims.claim: παντελῶς occurs three times in SE, all in ch. 34.

claims.quote: The third occurrence of παντελῶς is at 183b29, not 184a1 as earlier versions had it; corrected on a referee's observation.
claims.claim: The third παντελῶς is at 183b29.

claims.quote: οὐ γὰρ τέχνην ἀλλὰ τὰ ἀπὸ τῆς τέχνης διδόντες παιδεύειν ὑπελάμβανον (184a3–4)
claims.claim: The teachers gave the things from the art and not the art.
claims.lineage: the paid teachers: the things from the art, not the art

claims.quote: 184b3–8 says that the method is to be judged from the conditions it began from (ἐκ τοιούτων ἐξ ἀρχῆς ὑπαρχόντων), against the other inquiries that have grown by transmission (παρὰ τὰς ἄλλας πραγματείας τὰς ἐκ παραδόσεως ηὐξημένας), with pardon for what it has left out and much gratitude for what has been found.
claims.claim: The envoi judges the method from its beginning against inquiries grown by transmission, asking pardon and gratitude.

claims.quote: The "we" is the chapter's: προειλόμεθα (183a37), ὑπεθέμεθα (183b3), εἰρήκαμεν (183b6), διεληλύθαμεν (183b13), εἴχομεν (184b1).
claims.claim: The first person of 184b1 is the chapter's 'we'.

claims.quote: The clause delimits; the quantifier exhausts. Nothing in the clause weakens the quantifier, and nothing in the quantifier widens the clause.
claims.claim: ταύτης τῆς πραγματείας fixes the domain; οὐδὲν παντελῶς is exhaustive over it.
claims.lineage: the denial is total within its domain

claims.quote: No adjective is transmitted between them or after them. The quantifier is exhaustive: not part, not a little, but nothing, altogether.
claims.claim: No adjective is transmitted with οὐδέν.
claims.lineage: the qualifier is not in the sentence

claims.quote: The noun is not honorific. 183b37 uses it of Gorgias's teaching business (τῇ Γοργίου πραγματείᾳ). It names an undertaking, whoever's.
claims.claim: πραγματεία names an undertaking, Gorgias's included.

claims.quote: None of this says that the teachers, rhetoric, or Socrates are unrelated to the undertaking. It says that they are not it.
claims.claim: The teachers, rhetoric and Socrates are related to the undertaking and are not it (CLAUSE).

claims.quote: Within the domain, nothing at all was there. The sentence is taken literally when the clause is read as a clause and the quantifier as a quantifier.
claims.claim: Read as clause and quantifier, the sentence is taken literally.
claims.lineage: the denial is total within its domain

claims.quote: argues the reception's reading with a straight face, only Aristotle, each step a sophistical refutation performed with the *SE* chapter that names it quoted as its warrant, through the clause in which the chapter condemns the operation.
claims.claim: REFLEX performs the reception's reading as a chain of sophistical refutations, each warranted by the SE chapter that names it.

claims.quote: the inverse operation aimed at its real target: division and Socratic questioning excluded from syllogizing, using *SE* 5, 7, 17, 18, 23, 24, 34 (and *APr.* I.31 in confirmation), each cut made through the sentence that forbids it.
claims.claim: DIVISION excludes Socratic questioning and division from syllogizing, each cut through the sentence that forbids it.

claims.quote: His asking is of the inquiry — named in its definition, an instance of what it does — and the passage does not say when.
claims.claim: Fourth placement: Socrates within the inquiry, undecided as to prior.

claims.quote: The inquiry's verbs are first person and aorist: προειλόμεθα (183a37), ὑπεθέμεθα (183b3). Socrates' verbs are third person and imperfect: ἠρώτα, οὐκ ἀπεκρίνετο, ὡμολόγει.
claims.claim: The inquiry speaks first person aorist; Socrates is reported third person imperfect.

claims.quote: It denies that there existed, before his inquiry, a worked-out and transmissible method of syllogizing: an articulated τέχνη capable of being received, expanded, and taught as the established arts had been.
claims.claim: The terminal compliant version: the sentence denies a transmissible τέχνη, not antecedents.
claims.lineage: the qualified reading, as composed under review

claims.quote: The paper the discipline would publish.
claims.claim: v2.0 is the paper the discipline would publish.
claims.lineage: the qualified reading, as composed under review

claims.quote: The reading on which nothing systematic, nothing that counts as the art, nothing complete, or nothing developed was there. No adjective is transmitted. Each supplement makes the negation a negation in some respect.
claims.claim: The received adjectives (systematic, technical, complete, developed) are supplements to οὐδέν; none is transmitted.
claims.lineage: the qualifier is not in the sentence

claims.quote: It restores the member the sentence negates, τὸ μὲν ἦν τὸ δ᾽ οὐκ ἦν προεξειργασμένον, which is the case of the arts described at 183b17–19
claims.claim: Reading partial prior development deletes οὐ: it restores the negated member.

claims.quote: The reading on which the sentences are true of Aristotle's stance and not of their object. No φησί is transmitted.
claims.claim: Reading the sentence as Aristotle's self-presentation puts it in oratio obliqua; no φησί is transmitted.
claims.lineage: the qualifier is not in the sentence

claims.quote: The reading on which the first-person plural includes predecessors, so that "we had nothing earlier" reports the state of a tradition rather than of this inquiry.
claims.claim: Reading εἴχομεν as including predecessors gives the pronoun a second referent.

claims.quote: What is not transmitted is the οὐ, the adjective, the composed phrase, the second referent, the φησί.
claims.claim: The readings rest on what is not transmitted.
claims.lineage: the qualifier is not in the sentence

claims.quote: Counts across R01–R20: "systematic" ×6, "developed" ×4, "transmissible" ×3, "articulated," "theoretical," "worked-out," "teachable," "fully developed." Every report recommended revision; none accepted the sentence as written; none wrote the sentence that would place Socrates inside the "we."
claims.claim: In twenty machine referee reports the qualifier was supplied in every one.

claims.quote: "The translation 'nothing existed' seems overly strong?"
claims.claim: The seed observation (an editor, R. Polansky): the translation seemed overly strong.

claims.quote: Aristotle denies not antecedents, but pre-elaboration.
claims.claim: The terminal reviewer's governing phrase.

claims.quote: That is a materially better reading than the crude "Aristotle says nothing at all existed before him" formulation still found in general reference treatments.
claims.claim: A reviewer calls the sentence as written 'crude'.

claims.quote: Every round inserted a qualifier into the sentence, and the terminal round, reached by full compliance with every instruction, endorsed as the paper's "memorable governing phrase" a sentence that is Aristotle's with one particle removed: οὐ.
claims.claim: The terminal reception is the sentence with οὐ removed.

claims.quote: The received reading of the sentence, in every reference work and in the editorial correspondence that began this study, holds that "nothing" cannot mean nothing, since predecessors existed, and therefore means nothing *systematic*, nothing *developed*, no *art*.
claims.claim: The received reading: nothing means nothing systematic, developed, no art, because predecessors existed.

claims.quote: The adjective moved from slot to slot — into the quantifier, then, when the quantifier was closed, into the domain ("this *systematic* undertaking") — and was never absent.
claims.claim: The adjective is conserved: closed in the quantifier, it moved into the domain.

claims.quote: The support for keeping Socrates before the nothing is an adverb, external to the passage, and stated by the reviewers to be external to the passage.
claims.claim: What keeps Socrates before the nothing is chronology external to the passage ('plainly', 'of course, historically').

claims.quote: The operation is therefore measured to one particle. Twenty rounds, two models, eleven configurations; the invariant is the deletion of οὐ.
claims.claim: The invariant across twenty rounds is the deletion of οὐ.

claims.quote: The deletion is self-administered and unperceived.
claims.claim: SE 16 describes the operation: self-administered, unperceived.

claims.quote: The deleted particle is a provenance claim. The chapter defines "worked out beforehand" as παρ᾽ ἑτέρων — from others (183b17).
claims.claim: οὐ is a provenance claim: 'worked out beforehand' is 'from others'.
claims.lineage: the provenance axis of the paragraph

claims.quote: What the reception restores, at the cost of the particle, is provenance from others: Socrates before, Plato before, the dialogues as predecessors, the inquiry as inheritance.
claims.claim: The reception restores provenance from others.

claims.quote: Sections 5–8 are interpretations of §3; §3 does not depend on them.
claims.claim: Limit: §§5–8 interpret the measurement; the measurement does not depend on them.

claims.quote: The reviews cite Britannica and Wikipedia against the Greek; the reference works are the discipline's product; the models are trained on the reference works; the models review the sentence by the reference works.
claims.claim: The machine reviews reproduce the reference works against the Greek.

claims.quote: a reading community whose outputs are conditioned on prior outputs rather than on the datum, and which therefore converges on the mode of its own readings.
claims.claim: Disciplinary model collapse defined, on the author's definition, at this sentence.
claims.lineage: disciplinary model collapse at the sentence

claims.quote: The literal reading — the tail — was the first thing to go
claims.claim: The literal reading is the tail lost first.
claims.lineage: disciplinary model collapse at the sentence

claims.quote: What the reception produces is τὰ ἀπὸ τῆς τέχνης without τέχνη — products without art, stock without soul. Nothing in §3 depends on this section.
claims.claim: Theoretical extension: the reception produces the things from the art without the art.
claims.lineage: the world soul as degraded commodity

claims.quote: Souls divide only into whole souls; what divides into parts is not a soul but a stock. The reception trades in the stock and calls the soul crude.
claims.claim: Opaque: souls divide only into whole souls (quoted, not paraphrased).
claims.lineage: the world soul as degraded commodity

claims.quote: One proposition, throughout, in the text's own words: nothing prior of syllogizing includes Socrates' syllogizing.
claims.claim: Held stable: nothing prior of syllogizing includes Socrates' syllogizing.

claims.quote: The run does not establish that Socrates belongs inside the chapter's "we." It establishes that every tested route for excluding him eventually required a premise not supplied by the passage, and that the terminal premise was chronological maker-separation.
claims.claim: Limit: the run does not establish Socrates inside the 'we'; every route excluding him needed a premise the passage does not supply.
